newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Saudi Arabia deports 76 Indian girls.
newsitem.headline: India says Saudi Arabia deports 76 Indian girls.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has deported at least 76 Indian girls aged between five and 14, many handicapped and apparently used as beggars by their parents, police said on Tuesday.
The girls, who arrived in Bombay late on Monday, were sent to a remand home and an uncertain future. Police said their next task would be to locate the children's parents.
"They have no papers with them," a police official told Reuters. "We have been told to detain them and put them up in a remand home."
Police said most of the girls were the children of migrants who stayed on in Saudi Arabia after their visas expired and had since been deported.
An official at the Saudi consulate in Bombay said he was unaware of any deportation orders.
Shohara Bano, 10, said she was taken by her father to Mecca and was told to beg. "My father was caught by Saudi police and was sent away. They caught me later," she told reporters.
Police said a large number of the children were from India's eastern state of West Bengal.
The children were fed by police before being sent to the remand home in central Bombay's crowded Dongri area.
"The smaller ones promptly went to sleep after being fed with biscuits and tea on arrival. They are too young to understand what has happened to them," said a woman police constable.
Police said the Indian High Commission in Saudi Arabia had earlier issued emergency certificates to the children so that they could be allowed back home.
Police suspect that most of the handicapped children were made to beg during the Haj pilgrimage in Mecca when hundreds of thousands of Moslem faithful gather in the holy city.
Rubina, 10, showed the stump of her right hand. She said a relative had made her beg. "My wrist was cut off a year ago by a doctor," she said. "They told me I had developed something bad in my palm."
A police official said two Moslem women, who arrived on the same flight as the children, had been held for questioning.
Gulf countries have in that last few months deported tens of thousands of migrant workers, mostly from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Philippines.
